([[Henderson, Nevada]]) | college = | career_start = 2021 | years1 = [[2021–22 NBA G League season|2021]]–present | team1 = [[NBA G League Ignite]] | highlights = * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2021 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2021]]) * [[Jordan Brand Classic]] (2021) * [[Nike Hoop Summit]] (2021) }} '''Jaden Hardy''' (born July 5, 2002) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[NBA G League Ignite]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of top players in the 2021 class. ==Early life and high school career== Hardy and his family moved to Nevada from [[Detroit|Detroit, Michigan]] prior to high school.{{cite web |last1=Richey |first1=Scott |title=Las Vegas to C-U connection? Underwood all in on Hardy |url=https://www.news-gazette.com/sports/illini-sports/las-vegas-to-c-u-connection-underwood-all-in-on-hardy/article_1799aab6-20ab-58ad-b870-4cff08357aed.html |website=[[The News-Gazette (Champaign–Urbana)|The News-Gazette]] |access-date=April 19, 2021 |date=May 7, 2018}} He attended [[Coronado High School (Nevada)|Coronado High School]] in [[Henderson, Nevada]]. As a junior, Hardy averaged 30.4 points, 9.1 rebounds and 8.4 assists per game, earning Nevada [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]] and ''[[Las Vegas Review-Journal]]'' Boys Athlete of the Year honors.{{cite web |last1=Grimala |first1=Mike |title=Two prep athletes who dominated the competition |url=https://lasvegassun.com/news/2020/may/24/two-prep-athletes-who-dominated-the-competition/ |website=[[Las Vegas Sun]] |access-date=April 19, 2021 |date=May 24, 2020}}{{cite web |last1=Orts |first1=Jason |title=Nevada Preps awards — Boys Athlete of the Year |url=https://www.reviewjournal.com/nevada-preps/np-basketball/boys-basketball/nevada-preps-awards-boys-athlete-of-the-year-2038791/ |website=[[Las Vegas Review-Journal]] |access-date=April 19, 2021 |date=May 29, 2020}} On January 8, 2021, he opted out from the remainder of his senior season.{{cite web |last1=Jordan |first1=Jason |title=SI99 No. 1 SG Jaden Hardy No Longer Playing This Season |url=https://www.si.com/college/recruiting/basketball/jaden-hardy-coronado-si99-2021-not-playing-high-school |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=April 19, 2021 |date=January 8, 2021}} He was named to the rosters for the [[2021 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American Game]], [[Jordan Brand Classic]] and [[Nike Hoop Summit]].{{cite web |last1=Brewer |first1=Ray |title=Even without season, Coronado's Jaden Hardy named McDonald's All-American |url=https://lasvegassun.com/news/2021/feb/23/even-without-season-coronados-jaden-hardy-named-mc/ |website=[[Las Vegas Sun]] |access-date=April 19, 2021 |date=February 23, 2021}} ===Recruiting=== Hardy was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2021 class. Most recruiting analysts predicted that he would play professionally instead of attending college, with [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] and [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]] being his most likely college destinations.{{cite web |last1=Roberts |first1=Ben |title=More buzz indicating a top Kentucky basketball target will skip college for the pros |url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-recruiting/next-cats-blog/article250141824.html |website=[[Lexington Herald-Leader]] |access-date=April 19, 2021 |date=March 23, 2021}} On May 15, 2021, he announced that he would join the [[NBA G League]], forgoing college basketball. He chose the G League over offers from [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] and [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]], among others. {{College Athlete Recruit
